title: How to Convert HEIC to JPG on iPhone
description: Convert an existing HEIC photo to a JPEG copy on iPhone, check the actual file format and keep the original.
direct: A site wants JPG but your photo is HEIC? Make a JPEG copy of the existing photo. Changing the camera setting only affects future shots.
figureAlt: A site wants JPG but your photo is HEIC? Make a JPEG copy of the existing photo. Changing the camera setting only affects future shots.
cards.existing.heading: Already have the photo?
cards.existing.body: Convert or share a JPEG copy. Keep the HEIC original.
cards.future.heading: Only changing new shots?
cards.future.body: Camera → Formats → Most Compatible records future photos as JPEG.
sections.explicit.heading: Need a JPEG saved on the iPhone?
sections.explicit.body: Our PhotoFix app supports HEIC to JPEG, including batches. Select your photos, choose the HEIC-to-JPEG task, then inspect the exported copies. Check the current store listing for access and purchase options.
sections.mac.heading: Have a Mac? Use the built-in export
sections.mac.body: Open the HEIC in Preview or Photos, choose File → Export and select JPEG. Renaming .HEIC to .JPG does not convert the image.
sections.preserve.heading: Keep the original
sections.preserve.body: JPEG uses compression; it does not restore lost detail or guarantee a smaller file. Confirm the copy’s dimensions, appearance and file type. Review location metadata before sharing. Switching Camera → Formats → Most Compatible does not convert photos already in your library.
sources.apple-sharing.label: Apple: photo sharing formats
sources.apple-convert.label: Apple: converting HEIF media
related.hdr.label: HDR photo brightness is a different issue
steps.select.text: In Photos, open the picture and tap Share, then Options.
steps.share.text: Choose Most Compatible where available, then share a copy. Apple says files may convert to JPEG.
steps.check.text: Check the received file’s type or extension before uploading. If it is still HEIC, export an explicit JPEG copy.
